title: Funstra
tagline: An isometric sandbox RPG prototype about surviving a damaged port city — developed in the open, by agents, one playable demo at a time.

honesty.heading: Be clear about what this is
honesty.lede: Funstra is a development project that publishes its work as playable builds. It is not a finished game, it is not for sale, and it is not trying to look further along than it is.
is: A playable prototype. Each demo is a real Windows executable you can run for an hour, not a trailer or a wishlist page.
Free and MIT-licensed, source and all. Clone it, build it, take it apart.
Built by AI agents against a written vision, design and world bible, with every build validated by an automated harness before it ships.
Original work — procedural geometry and sound, no purchased assets, no external services required to play.

Honest about its reviews. Four reviewer agents inspect guided runs of the actual build, screenshots, logs, the manual and source. Their verdicts are published unedited, with the limits of that method stated.
isNot: A finished sandbox campaign. The current demo is a single neighbourhood and roughly an hour of content.
A commercial release. There is no store page, no price, no roadmap you have paid for.
A finished environment. The stylized art is intentional; useful spaces, richer interactions and an expandable map are the next development priority.
A live world. Nothing simulates while the application is closed, and the economy is small on purpose.
Stable across versions. Saves may carry forward, but a demo can and does change underneath you.

panelNote: Four reviewer agents each awarded Demo 03 8/10 for different reasons. These are guided build reviews, supported by logs, screenshots and source inspection, rather than exploratory human play or independent acceptance of later fixes.

pipeline.desc: An agent implements a demo against VISION, DESIGN and WORLD, then runs the rules and runtime harness.
Tools/Release.ps1 drives a batch-mode Unity build, verifies the executable and zips the portable package.
The same script opens a tagged GitHub Release and uploads the zip — one command, no console.
Publishing the release fires a GitHub Actions workflow that regenerates this site from the live release list and deploys it to GitHub Pages.
The download below is whatever the newest release is. Nobody edits this page by hand.
